description: Iteration-1's FIND-006 fix wrapped relay_quote()/read_solana_balance_usd() production wiring in try/except so a transient failure fails closed with a clean JSON line + ledger row instead of an uncaught crash, matching the module's own documented output contract (franklin_sol_base_refill.py:28-29: 'exactly one JSON line on stdout... non-zero otherwise'). That same protection was not extended to every effectful call reachable in run_refill(): deps['append_ledger'](...) is invoked from every single refusal path via the shared `fail()` closure (franklin_sol_base_refill.py:174-179) plus five more call sites (lines ~301, ~334-345, ~423, ~442, ~458) with NO surrounding try/except anywhere in the function, and deps['is_killed']() (line 181) is likewise unwrapped. In production wiring (build_default_deps, lines 469-525), append_ledger ultimately calls lib/ledger.py's append_ledger(path, row), which performs `os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)` and `open(path, 'a', ...)` (lib/ledger.py:34-38) -- a disk-full or permissions failure there raises uncaught. Since `fail()` itself calls `deps['append_ledger']` as its FIRST action on every refusal path (line 178), a disk/permission failure at that exact moment -- which is precisely when the module is trying to record a money-safety refusal -- crashes the whole process with a Python traceback, printing NO JSON line at all and leaving zero audit trail, which is strictly worse than any of the seven scenarios iteration-1's FIND-006 fix already addressed (those all still successfully wrote a failure row before this gap).

crossReference.specRequirement: franklin_sol_base_refill.py:28-29 module docstring ("Output: exactly one JSON line on stdout... non-zero otherwise")
crossReference.relatedFinding: iteration-1 FIND-006 (fixed relay_quote/read_solana_balance_usd only, not append_ledger itself)
